clue.text: Tell of soldier getting fresh

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier in crosswords
late can mean recent or newly come, as in the late news, so fresh

explanation.surface: Someone recounts the tale of a soldier who became cheeky with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' suggests impudence, but it is used in the sense of recent; RE is the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate something is to narrate it, a synonym for telling of it.

clue.text: Queen 'arassed Tubby

parts.note: R is Regina, Latin for queen
harassed means hounded; the apostrophe drops the H, as in Cockney speech

explanation.surface: A harassed queen, in Cockney accent, is described as plump.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'arassed signals a dropped H, so the synonym hounded loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounded and tubby both describe a plump, chubby shape.

clue.text: Students keeping primate in a flap

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the students enclose the primate

parts.note: L is a learner driver, so two Ls are students
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: Students holding an ape are in a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a flap' looks like a state of panic, but 'flap' is the definition, a fold of a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapel is the folded-back flap on the front of a jacket or coat.

clue.text: English coastal visitor changes colour

parts.note: turns means changes, as leaves turn in autumn
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A tourist on the English shore changes colour, perhaps from sunburn.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'visitor' is a bird: the turnstone is a wading bird that winters on English shores.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnstone is a migratory shore bird that visits British coasts, flipping pebbles for food.

clue.text: Support for member concerning cheese

parts.note: a stilt is a pole that supports a leg, a limb or member
on means about or concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: A prop for a limb is somehow linked to a cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' is a limb here, the leg a stilt holds up. STILTON is a strong English blue cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a famous English blue-veined variety, an example of the general category named.

clue.text: Clients designed template

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters are laid out to a new plan

explanation.surface: Customers drew up a pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut-out sheet used as a pattern for reproducing shapes.

clue.text: Angry plagiarist loses patience, initially

indicators.note: loses says a letter is taken away from the word for a plagiarist

parts.note: a pirate copies others' work without permission

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of patience

explanation.surface: A plagiarist runs out of patience and gets cross.
explanation.walkthrough: PIRATE, one who pirates others' work, drops P.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone irate is furious or incensed, simply very cross.

clue.text: Supply lock for siren

parts.note: a supply teacher is a temp, standing in for an absent one
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A request to provide a lock for a seductress.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a supply teacher is a temporary stand-in, so supply means temp.
explanation.definitionFit: A siren is a seductive woman who lures men, as does a temptress.

clue.text: Features and assembly of tea urn

indicators.note: assembly of means putting these letters together in a new order

explanation.surface: Putting together a tea urn has its characteristics.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's nature is their essential qualities or character, their defining traits.

clue.text: Incentive for a bishop to get into bed

indicators.note: to get into puts the pieces inside the word for a bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: An inducement offered to a bishop to climb into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To get into' signals the container. A bishop is styled the Right Reverend.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is a reward offered as inducement, from the carrot dangled before a donkey.

clue.text: Stimulant given to patient of a certain type

parts.note: an upper is slang for a stimulant drug
a doctor's case is a patient being treated

explanation.surface: A patient is handed a pep pill of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' is printing type: capitals are the upper-case letters, originally kept in the upper case of a compositor's tray.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper-case describes capital letters, a particular kind of printing type.

clue.text: Allow Dutch money to be invested in island

indicators.note: something invested in another is placed inside it, so these letters go within

parts.note: an ait is a small river island
DM is the Deutschmark; Dutch once meant German, from Deutsch

explanation.surface: Permission to put Dutch currency into an island's economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be invested in' signals the container; 'Dutch' is the old English word for German, from Deutsch.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to let them in, a synonym for allow.

clue.text: Winter transport carrying Oscar back to island

indicators.note: back says the whole assembled piece is read from right to left
a vehicle carrying a load holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a sled travels over snow in winter
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sleigh brings Oscar home to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: O inside SLED makes SOLED, which 'back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Delos is a small Greek island in the Cyclades, birthplace of Apollo in myth.

clue.text: Revolutionary appears in register in New York

indicators.note: one piece appearing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: a roster is a list or register of names
Che Guevara is the crossword's standard revolutionary

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's name shows up on a list kept in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appears in' signals the container. The definition names a place found in New York State.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochester is a city in western New York State, so it is a place in that state.

clue.text: Deal makes detective buy a round

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
a shout is informal for buying a round of drinks, your shout

explanation.surface: A detective strikes a bargain by paying for everyone's drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shout' is British and Australian slang for one's turn to buy the drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To dish out is to distribute or hand out, as one deals cards.

clue.text: Despatched to protect a crowd in ceremony

indicators.note: to protect means to surround, so the outer word wraps the others

parts.note: despatched means sent off
cram means to crowd or pack in

explanation.surface: Sent off to guard a throng at a ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To protect' signals the container: the despatched word wraps the others like a guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrament is a religious ceremony such as baptism or communion.

clue.text: Advocate having wife in bed

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for wife inside the word for a bed

parts.note: a layer is a bed, as in a bed of rock

explanation.surface: A barrister keeps his wife in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed' is a stratum, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and elsewhere an advocate is a legal pleader, a synonym for a solicitor or barrister.

clue.text: Featherweight champion appears between working days

parts.note: something featherweight is very small, wee
a knight was a champion who fought for a cause or lady

explanation.surface: A boxing featherweight champion appears in midweek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Featherweight' suggests boxing but means tiny. A knight was a champion in medieval combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A weeknight falls between two working days, any evening from Monday to Thursday.

clue.text: Swallow mushroom during execution

indicators.note: during puts the fungus inside the word for execution, as an event within a span

parts.note: an act is a deed or execution of something
a cep is an edible boletus mushroom

explanation.surface: Someone gulps down a mushroom while being put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Execution' is the carrying out of a deed, not a hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow a claim is to believe or take it on board, a sense of accepting.

clue.text: Quite a few keeping Bob dry

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the number encloses the coin

parts.note: thirty is quite a few
a bob is an old British shilling, abbreviated S

explanation.surface: A good number keep Bob from drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was a shilling in old British money, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry means needing a drink, a synonym for parched.

clue.text: Lady's maid found showing off in the kitchen

definitions.meaning: a servant who helps her mistress put on her clothes
a sideboard with shelves that displays plates and crockery in a kitchen

explanation.surface: A maid is spotted parading herself in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a servant who helps someone get dressed and a kitchen cabinet with open display shelves.

clue.text: Falsify and lie, leading to dismissal

indicators.note: to falsify is to alter or doctor, so the letters are tampered with

explanation.surface: Lying and deceit end in someone being sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading to' is a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismissal of a claim is rejection of it, as is a denial.

clue.text: Book store

definitions.meaning: to book is to arrange in advance, hold a table
a store is a stock kept back for future use

explanation.surface: A book shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to arrange ahead, such as a seat, and a supply set aside.

clue.text: Violin fitted with new string

indicators.note: fitted with means the violin has the new letter set inside it

parts.note: a Strad is a Stradivarius violin

explanation.surface: A violin gets a fresh string.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a single thread or string.

clue.text: Tory leader went mad with Scot — an actor

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: raged means went mad with fury
Ian is the typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A Conservative chief flew into a rage alongside a Scottish performer.
explanation.walkthrough: IAN is a stock Scottish name in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who specialises in tragic roles.

clue.text: Old-time artist made redundant

parts.note: ex means former or old, and T is time
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter from the old days loses his job.
explanation.walkthrough: EX (former) plus T (time) plus RA, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts. 'Made' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means surplus to requirements, a synonym for superfluous.

clue.text: African emperor having information about America

indicators.note: about turns the word for information round so it reads backwards

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
US is the United States

explanation.surface: An Ethiopian ruler possesses details about America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning' but signals the turnaround, making NEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus was the title of the Ethiopian ruler, and the emperor was Negusa Nagast, king of kings.

clue.text: Board hit it off

definitions.meaning: to board a bus or train is to climb aboard
to hit it off is to be friendly with someone

explanation.surface: A committee became fast friends.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to climb aboard and to have a good relationship.

clue.text: Period with conservationists is a factor

parts.note: an age is a period of time
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: An era of green campaigners proves an important influence.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust conserves historic houses and land in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean a person who acts on another's behalf, or a cause that produces an effect.

clue.text: Son has convulsions seeing carnage

parts.note: convulsions of laughter are fits of laughing

explanation.surface: A boy has fits on seeing a massacre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Convulsions' suggests a medical fit, but it is fits of mirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughter and carnage both mean the large-scale killing of people.

clue.text: Song about an aromatic plant

indicators.note: about means going round, so the song encloses the article

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: A song tells of a fragrant herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Dittany is a fragrant herb of the mint family, from Crete.

clue.text: Awkward ascent in carriage

indicators.note: awkward suggests the letters sit clumsily and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy climb made in a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' is not a coach but bearing, how one holds oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage can mean posture or bearing, as can the way someone stands.
